new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0747776
--- /dev/null
+++ b/work/check_str.py
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+import io
+
+s = io.StringIO()
+print('str type:', type(s))
+print('has write attr:', hasattr(type(s), 'write'))
+mro = type(s).__mro__
+print('MRO:')
+for b in mro:
+    print(f'  {b}: write in __dict__? {"write" in b.__dict__}')
+
+# Test _check_methods from the project
+import sys
+sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace')
+from pysnooper.utils import _check_methods, WritableStream
+result = _check_methods(type(s), 'write')
+print('_check_methods result:', result)
+print('isinstance check:', isinstance(s, WritableStream))
diff --git a/work/check_str2.py b/work/check_str2.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..245ffb8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/work/check_str2.py
@@ -0,0 +1,24 @@
+import sys
+sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace')
+
+from pysnooper.utils import _check_methods, WritableStream
+import io
+
+s = io.StringIO()
+C = type(s)
+
+# Debug the subclasshook step by step
+mro = C.__mro__
+print(f"C = {C}")
+for B in mro:
+    v = 'write' in B.__dict__
+    val = B.__dict__.get('write', '<NOT FOUND>') if v else 'N/A'
+    print(f"  B={B}, has write?={v}, value is None?={val is None if hasattr(val, '__class__') else 'no'}")
+
+result = _check_methods(C, 'write')
+print(f"_check_methods result: {result}")
+print(f"isinstance(s, WritableStream): {isinstance(s, WritableStream)}")
+
+# Now try to understand what's going wrong by checking write directly
+wr = s.__class__.__dict__['write']
+print(f"write from class __dict__: {wr}, type={type(wr)}, is None: {wr is None}")
